definitions.explanation: An electrically powered device with rotating blades that creates airflow to cool a room or provide ventilation.

examples.japanese: {扇風機|せんぷうき}をつけて。
{扇風機|せんぷうき}の{風|かぜ}が{気持|きも}ちいい。
examples.english: The breeze from the fan feels nice.

examples.japanese: {暑|あつ}いので{扇風機|せんぷうき}をつけた。
examples.english: It was hot, so I turned on the fan.

examples.japanese: {夏|なつ}は{扇風機|せんぷうき}とエアコンを{一緒|いっしょ}に{使|つか}っている。
examples.english: In summer, I use the fan and air conditioner together.

examples.japanese: {寝|ね}る{時|とき}に{扇風機|せんぷうき}をつけたまま{寝|ね}ると、{朝|あさ}{起|お}きた{時|とき}に{体|からだ}がだるくなることがある。
examples.english: If you leave the fan on while sleeping, you might feel sluggish when you wake up in the morning.

notes:
{扇風機|せんぷうき} is the standard word for an electric fan. The word combines {扇|せん} (fan) + {風|ふう} (wind) + {機|き} (machine).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {扇風機|せんぷうき}をつける/かける: to turn on a fan
- {扇風機|せんぷうき}を{消|け}す/とめる: to turn off a fan
- {扇風機|せんぷうき}の{風|かぜ}: the breeze from a fan
- {首振|くびふ}り{扇風機|せんぷうき}: oscillating fan

RELATED TERMS:
- エアコン: air conditioner (cools more effectively)
- {換気扇|かんきせん}: ventilation/exhaust fan (used in kitchens and bathrooms)
- {団扇|うちわ}: flat hand fan (traditional)
- {扇子|せんす}: folding fan

CULTURAL NOTE:
There is a well-known urban legend in Japan about "fan death" ({扇風機|せんぷうき}の{都市伝説|としでんせつ}), though it is more associated with Korea. Many Japanese people avoid sleeping with a fan blowing directly on them.
